content:
Webb County commissioners have put a proposed office building on the former Rock House site on hold while the county works out which offices need room and where, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The proposal was tabled after commissioners reviewed a feasibility study for the county-owned property at 918 and 920 Houston St. in downtown Laredo, the Times reported.

The study laid out three options, all based on preliminary budget estimates rather than construction bids: a one-story, 6,028-square-foot office estimated at $2.3 million to $2.6 million; a two-story, 19,131-square-foot office estimated at $7.2 million to $8.4 million; and a 23-space parking lot estimated at about $230,000. A lot would not be required if the county built either office, according to the study.

The study named County Administration, the Budget Office and Civil/Legal as possible occupants, along with future departments. It left the final mix of departments, the building's size and height, parking and the budget for a later phase, which would start with architectural and engineering design if the county decides to build.

Precinct 4 Commissioner Ricardo Jaime and Precinct 3 Commissioner John Galo sit on the county's Buildings Assessment Committee, which is working with another architect on a countywide look at how departments should be housed. Jaime said committing to a permanent plan for the site before that work is done would be irresponsible, and that the county should base the decision on need rather than want, according to the Times. Galo agreed the committee should settle the space question before the court approves a building.

Jaime noted that the county has room elsewhere, citing the former sheriff's administration building, where some departments have asked to settle permanently, the Billy Hall Administration Building remodel, and the Fesco Building purchase, which has already moved some departments.

The lots were cleared after the county decided that saving the old Rock House was not worth the expense. In December 2025, Jaime said architects put restoration at roughly $3 million for construction plus about $300,000 for design.

What to watch next: the committee's countywide space review, and whether the county moves the Rock House site into a design phase — and at what size and cost — once that review is done.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, “Webb County reassesses future of former Rock House site,” October 28, 2026

title: Webb County pauses Rock House site plans while it reviews office space needs
